root_cause.text: The `sev_es_sync_vmsa()` function did not check whether the vCPU had already been launched (i.e., the VMSA was already encrypted), allowing a write to guest-private memory that causes an RMP violation panic on SNP-capable hosts.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (vcpu->arch.guest_state_protected) return -EINVAL;` to `sev_es_sync_vmsa()`. The CVE description and commit message state that the flaw existed since commit ad73109ae7ec but only became actively dangerous with SNP support, and the call trace shows the panic occurring in `sev_es_sync_vmsa` called from `snp_launch_update_vmsa`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Guard against VMSA sync when guest state is already protected to avoid invalid operations.
intent_record.what: Added an early return -EINVAL check in sev_es_sync_vmsa if vcpu->arch.guest_state_protected is true.
intent_record.how: Prevents the VMSA synchronization from executing when the guest state is already protected, returning an error immediately.
